findings.element: Shopify stores card, step 2 "Created product should be: Inventory" with Open Settings
findings.finding: "Created product", "Inventory" and "Non-inventory" are QuickBooks item-type jargon, and nothing on screen says what the setting does or why stock sync needs it — yet it is the one step blocking Enable.
findings.user_impact: A first-timer can't tell whether changing a Synder setting in another tab will alter their existing products or their books, so they hesitate on a required step or abandon setup.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one line of helper text such as "So QuickBooks counts stock for products Synder adds. Your existing products and past transactions don't change." with a Learn more link.

evidence.quote: Now it is Non-inventory. Change it in Settings › My ceramic plates (Shopify) › Products/Services and click Update. This page updates by itself.

findings.element: Sync block, Disabled state, helper text above Enable
findings.finding: The Enable copy says only new changes are sent but never says that stock levels that already differ will stay different, even though the Stock check block on the same screen shows 2 products that differ.
findings.user_impact: The user assumes Enable makes Shopify match QuickBooks and treats the job as done (KF-2 pattern), so wrong Shopify stock stays wrong with no prompt to fix it.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the helper text: "Stock that already differs stays as it is — fix it in Stock check." and link it to the Stock check block.

evidence.quote: Sends to 1 ready store. Only changes made after you enable are sent.

findings.element: Reconcile tab, "Accept QuickBooks" action and its confirm dialog
findings.finding: "Accept QuickBooks" does not say it overwrites Shopify stock, and the confirm dialog adds more jargon ("on hand", "sync event") without saying whether the change can be undone.
findings.user_impact: A cautious owner afraid of overwriting real store counts either cancels and leaves the difference open, or clicks Ignore (which has no confirm) and the difference is just marked reviewed.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the dialog say "Shopify stock for Ceramic plate 24cm will change from 132 to 140 to match QuickBooks." and add how to reverse it (or say plainly it can't be undone).

evidence.quote: Shopify on hand for "Ceramic plate 24cm" in My ceramic plates will be set to 140 (change +8). A sync event will be created to apply it.
